examples.ko: 기내식으로 소고기와 생선 중에 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: For the in-flight meal, you can choose between beef and fish.
I ate the in-flight meal on the plane and fell asleep right away.
I was surprised that the in-flight meal was tastier than I expected.
Special in-flight meals must be requested in advance.
I also requested a vegetarian in-flight meal.

examples.ko: 짧은 비행에서는 기내식 대신 간식만 줘요.
examples.en: On short flights they only give snacks instead of a meal.

explain: '기내'는 비행기 안이라는 뜻이라서 '기내식'은 비행기에서 주는 식사예요. '기내식을 먹다, 기내식이 나오다'처럼 쓰고, 비행기 안에서 파는 간식이나 음료는 보통 '기내식'이라고 하지 않아요.

phrases.example: 이륙하고 한 시간 뒤에 기내식이 나와요.
phrases.en: The in-flight meal is served an hour after takeoff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식사가 제공될 때 '나오다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '나오다' is used when the meal is served.

phrases.en: I ordered a vegetarian in-flight meal in advance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특별한 식사를 미리 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking for a special meal ahead of time.

phrases.en: The in-flight meal on this plane is tastier than I expected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛을 평가하는 말과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with words that judge taste.

explain_en: '기내' means inside the plane, so '기내식' is the meal served on a flight. You say '기내식을 먹다' or '기내식이 나오다'. Snacks or drinks sold on board are not usually called '기내식'.

examples.en: I bought a fresh octopus at the market.
An octopus has eight arms.

examples.ko: 매운 낙지볶음을 먹고 물을 많이 마셨어요.
examples.en: I ate spicy stir-fried octopus and drank a lot of water.
The octopus is wriggling on the plate.
The octopus soup is refreshing.
Both octopus and squid are sea animals.

explain: '문어', '오징어'와 비슷하게 생겼지만 서로 다른 바다 동물이에요. 한국 요리에서는 낙지볶음과 연포탕이 잘 알려져 있어요.

phrases.en: I ate spicy stir-fried octopus.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낙지로 만든 대표적인 한국 요리 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of a well-known Korean dish made with octopus.

phrases.en: The live octopus is still moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산'은 살아 있다는 뜻이라서 살아 있는 낙지를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 산 means alive, so this is a live octopus.

phrases.en: I bought one octopus at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 낙지는 '마리'로 세므로 수를 말할 때 이렇게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Octopus is counted with 마리.

explain_en: It looks similar to the larger 문어 and to 오징어, but each is a different sea animal. In Korean cooking, 낙지볶음 and 연포탕 are well known.

examples.en: I blanch the spinach and toss it with sesame oil and salt.
Add the seasoning and gently toss it by hand.

examples.ko: 어머니가 배추 속에 고춧가루를 넣고 버무리고 계세요.
examples.en: Mom is mixing red pepper powder into the cabbage filling.
I toss the salad greens with dressing and eat them.

examples.ko: 오이를 소금에 절였다가 식초와 설탕에 버무렸어요.
examples.en: I salted the cucumber and then tossed it with vinegar and sugar.

examples.ko: 면을 삶은 다음 소스에 버무리면 돼요.
examples.en: Just boil the noodles and then toss them in the sauce.

explain: '섞다'보다 양념이나 소스가 골고루 묻도록 뒤적이는 느낌이에요. 나물을 양념에 섞을 때는 '무치다'도 많이 써요. 비슷하게 생긴 '얼버무리다'는 말을 분명하지 않게 할 때 쓰는 다른 단어예요.

phrases.en: I mix the vegetables with seasoning and eat them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에 버무리다'로 무엇과 섞는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '~에 버무리다' to say what you mix it with.

phrases.en: Please mix the sauce in evenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '골고루'와 함께 쓰면 양념이 전체에 묻게 섞는 느낌이 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 골고루, it clearly means mixing so the seasoning coats everything.

phrases.en: I season the spinach and eat it as a side dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나물을 양념에 섞을 때 '버무리다' 대신 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used instead of 버무리다 for seasoning vegetables.

explain_en: Cooking: coat food evenly with sauce or seasoning. Compared with '섞다' (to mix), it feels like turning ingredients so that seasoning or sauce coats them evenly. For vegetable side dishes, '무치다' is also commonly used. The similar-looking '얼버무리다' is a different word meaning to speak vaguely.

t90.ax: Add the seasoning and gently toss it by hand.

examples.en: How about budae-jjigae for lunch today?
I add ramen noodles to budae-jjigae when I eat it.

examples.ko: 친구들과 부대찌개를 끓여 먹으며 이야기를 했어요.
examples.en: I talked with my friends while boiling and eating budae-jjigae.
The budae-jjigae is bubbling away.

examples.ko: 이 집 부대찌개는 국물이 칼칼해서 맛있어요.
examples.en: This restaurant's budae-jjigae has a spicy broth and tastes good.

examples.ko: 부대찌개에 햄과 소시지가 듬뿍 들어 있어요.
examples.en: The budae-jjigae is full of ham and sausage.

explain: 햄, 소시지, 김치, 라면 등을 넣고 매콤하게 끓이는 찌개예요. 큰 냄비에 끓여 같이 먹는 음식이라 친구나 가족과 먹을 때 많이 시켜요. 라면 사리나 떡 사리를 추가하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I tried making budaejjigae at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찌개를 만들 때는 '끓이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 끓이다 for cooking a stew.

phrases.en: Two servings of budaejjigae, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 시킬 때 '인분'으로 양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: At a restaurant, you give the amount in servings (인분).

phrases.en: My friend and I ordered budaejjigae and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배달이나 식당에서 주문해서 먹을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for ordering it, by delivery or at a restaurant, and eating it.

explain_en: It is a spicy stew made with ham, sausage, kimchi, ramen and more. Since it is boiled in a big pot and shared, people often order it when eating with friends or family. You can also add extra ramen noodles or rice cakes.

en: to trim; to groom; to fix up

examples.en: I trim the trees in the garden on weekends.
I had my hair done at the salon yesterday.
I cleaned the fish and put it in the fridge.

examples.ko: 아버지가 손질한 칼은 아주 잘 들어요.
examples.en: The knife my father took care of cuts very well.

examples.ko: 내일 손님이 오니까 집 앞 화단을 손질할 거예요.
examples.en: A guest is coming tomorrow, so I will tidy the flower bed in front of the house.
After shaping my eyebrows, I looked in the mirror.

explain: 머리, 나무, 생선, 옷처럼 다듬거나 정리해야 하는 것에 두루 써요. 요리에서는 생선이나 채소를 씻고 자르는 준비 단계를 '손질하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My mother cleaned and prepped the fish she bought at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리하기 전에 씻고 자르는 준비를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means washing and cutting before cooking.

phrases.en: I put the prepared vegetables in the pot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 모양으로 이미 준비한 재료를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-ㄴ' form refers to ingredients that are already prepared.

phrases.en: I trimmed the trees in the yard on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 머리처럼 길이나 모양을 다듬을 때도 '손질하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '손질하다' is also used for trimming the shape or length of things like trees or hair.

explain_en: To neaten or repair something, including hair; general. It works for anything you tidy or shape: hair, trees, fish, clothes. In cooking, it names the prep step of cleaning and cutting fish or vegetables.

t90.ax: I had my hair done at the salon yesterday.

examples.ko: 원두커피 전문점이 우리 동네에 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new coffee shop specializing in brewed coffee opened in our neighborhood.
I brew my own coffee from beans every morning.
Brewed coffee has a stronger aroma than instant mix coffee.

examples.ko: 이 원두커피로 아이스 아메리카노를 만들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please make an iced Americano with this coffee.
How much is one cup of brewed coffee?
At the office I drink brewed coffee with milk in it.

explain: '믹스커피', '인스턴트커피'와 대비해서 원두를 갈아 내린 커피를 말해요. 카페에서 파는 커피는 보통 원두커피예요. 원두를 내리는 도구(드립, 머신)에 따라 맛이 달라져요.

phrases.en: On weekends I brew coffee and drink it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원두에 물을 부어 커피를 만들 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for making coffee by pouring water over ground beans.

phrases.en: One cup of brewed coffee, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페에서 주문할 때 바로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Something you can use right away when ordering at a cafe.

phrases.en: I stopped by a specialty coffee shop on my way home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원두로 내린 커피를 파는 가게를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a shop that sells coffee brewed from beans.

explain_en: It contrasts with '믹스커피' and '인스턴트커피' and means coffee brewed from ground beans. The coffee sold at cafes is usually this kind. The taste changes depending on how it is brewed, such as drip or machine.

examples.en: Cheonggukjang has a strong smell but tastes good.
I cooked cheonggukjang stew for dinner.
I add tofu and kimchi to the cheonggukjang.

examples.ko: 청국장을 먹고 나서 창문을 열어 환기했어요.
examples.en: After eating cheonggukjang, I opened the window to air out the room.
I tried cheonggukjang for the first time and it tasted nutty.
Cheonggukjang and a bowl of rice, please.

explain: 된장찌개와 비슷하게 끓여 먹지만 냄새가 훨씬 강해서 호불호가 갈려요. 식당에서는 '청국장찌개'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: I ordered cheonggukjang stew at the restaurant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당 메뉴에서 쓰는 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name used on restaurant menus.

phrases.en: The house is full of the smell of cheonggukjang.
phrases.nuance_ko: 청국장의 강한 냄새를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to talk about its strong smell.

phrases.en: I ate rice mixed with cheonggukjang.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥에 청국장을 넣고 비벼 먹는 방법이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes eating it mixed with rice.

explain_en: It is boiled like doenjang jjigae, but the smell is much stronger, so people either love it or dislike it. In restaurants it may be called '청국장찌개'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is learning addition and subtraction now.
Subtraction is a little harder than addition.
You can solve this problem by subtracting.

examples.ko: 거스름돈을 계산할 때 뺄셈 실력이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need subtraction skills to calculate change.

examples.ko: 아이가 뺄셈 문제를 하나도 안 틀렸어요.
examples.en: The child didn't get a single subtraction problem wrong.
Subtraction was hard, so I used a calculator.

explain: '덧셈', '곱셈', '나눗셈'과 함께 외우면 좋아요. 계산을 읽을 때는 '5 빼기 2는 3'처럼 '빼기'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Ten minus four is six.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계산을 소리 내어 읽을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when reading a calculation aloud.

phrases.en: I tried subtraction without a calculator.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계산하는 일을 말할 때 '하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 하다 for the act of calculating.

phrases.example: 숙제로 뺄셈 문제를 열 개 풀었어요.
phrases.en: For homework, I solved ten subtraction problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수학 숙제나 시험에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing common in math homework and tests.

explain_en: It is good to learn it together with '덧셈', '곱셈' and '나눗셈'. When reading out a calculation, you say '빼기', as in '5 빼기 2는 3'.

en: standard language; standard Korean; standard speech

examples.en: On the news, announcers always use standard Korean.

examples.ko: 저는 부산 사람이라 표준말이 조금 어색해요.
examples.en: I'm from Busan, so standard Korean feels a little awkward to me.
How are dialects and standard Korean different?
Let's check in the dictionary whether this word is standard.
I practice giving presentations in standard Korean every day.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구는 사투리보다 표준말이 더 알아듣기 쉽대요.
examples.en: My foreign friend says standard Korean is easier to understand than dialects.

explain: 사투리의 반대말로 많이 써요. 글이나 공식적인 자리에서는 '표준어'라고 하고, 일상 대화에서는 '표준말'이라고 편하게 말해요.

phrases.en: You must write in standard language on the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 공식적인 자리에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The term used in writing and formal settings.

phrases.en: I try to use standard Korean since I came to Seoul.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사투리 대신 표준말로 말한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means speaking in standard Korean instead of a dialect.

phrases.en: My grandmother speaks in dialect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표준말의 반대로 지역마다 다른 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 표준말: speech that differs by region.

explain_en: Everyday word for speaking standard Korean, e.g. on broadcasts. It is often used as the opposite of '사투리' (dialect). In writing or formal settings people say '표준어', while '표준말' is the more casual way to say it in everyday talk.

t90.ax: How are dialects and standard Korean different?

examples.en: I print my homework at school.

examples.ko: 이 파일을 열 장 프린트해 주세요.
examples.en: Please print ten copies of this file.
I printed the meeting materials in advance yesterday.
Check the font size before printing.
I can't print because there's no ink.
I put the printed paper on the desk.

explain: '인쇄하다'는 공식적인 말이고 '프린트하다'는 일상에서 더 편하게 써요. 명사로 '프린트'는 인쇄한 종이를 말하기도 해요(프린트를 나눠 주다). 사진을 종이로 뽑을 때는 '인화하다'나 '뽑다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I printed ten copies of the meeting materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: '프린트하다'보다 공식적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than 프린트하다.

phrases.en: I got a handout from the teacher in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '프린트'가 인쇄한 종이를 뜻할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here 프린트 means the printed paper itself.

phrases.en: Please print your homework and bring it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인쇄한 뒤에 가져오라고 할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Links printing and bringing in one sentence.

explain_en: Casual loanword; everyday printing of documents from a printer. 인쇄하다 is the formal word, 프린트하다 is the casual everyday one. The noun 프린트 can also mean the printed handout (프린트를 나눠 주다). For turning photos into prints, people say 인화하다 or 뽑다.

t90.ax: I print my homework at school.

examples.en: We raised our juice glasses and made a toast.
I make a toast to the new year with friends.
We all toasted and then ate cake.
The boss suggested that we toast first.

examples.ko: 축하하는 마음으로 건배하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see them toasting with congratulations in their hearts.
Is everyone ready to make a toast?

explain: 건배할 때는 '건배!'나 '위하여!'라고 외쳐요. 무엇을 위해 건배하는지는 '새해를 위하여'처럼 '-을/를 위하여'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Everyone raised their glasses and made a toast.
phrases.nuance_ko: '건배하다'와 뜻이 같고 '건배'를 따로 떼어 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 건배하다, with 건배 separated out.

phrases.en: We all shouted "Cheers!" together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잔을 부딪칠 때 외치는 말이에요. '위하여!'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you shout when clinking glasses; '위하여!' is also used.

phrases.en: We made a toast to the new year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-을/를 위하여'로 무엇을 위해 건배하는지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-을/를 위하여' says what you are toasting to.
phrases.en_equiv: to toast to the new year

explain_en: When toasting, people shout '건배!' or '위하여!'. To say what the toast is for, use '-을/를 위하여', as in '새해를 위하여'.

examples.en: My younger brother learns kendo after school.
Kendo values good manners very much.

examples.ko: 검도가 힘들어도 계속 해 볼 거예요.
examples.en: Even if kendo is hard, I will keep trying.
In kendo you shout loudly.

examples.ko: 검도와 태권도는 모두 몸과 마음을 키워 줘요.
examples.en: Both kendo and taekwondo build body and mind.
My dad is a kendo instructor.

explain: 죽도로 겨루는 무술이에요. 운동하는 곳은 '검도장'이고, 가르치는 사람은 '사범'이라고 해요. '검도를 하다', '검도를 배우다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I do kendo every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동을 한다고 말할 때 '하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '하다' to say that you do the sport.

phrases.en: The kendo gym is near the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검도를 하는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the place where kendo is practiced.

phrases.en: The kendo instructor showed me the posture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 검도를 가르치는 사람이에요. 높여서 '사범님'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: The person who teaches kendo; politely called '사범님'.

explain_en: Kendo is a martial art fought with bamboo swords. The place to practice is a '검도장', and the teacher is called a '사범'. You say '검도를 하다' or '검도를 배우다'.

examples.en: My younger sibling plays the drums in a band.

examples.ko: 드럼 소리가 너무 커서 이웃이 항의했어요.
examples.en: The drum sound was so loud that a neighbor complained.
I attend a drum academy.
This song starts with the drums.
The drums play a big role in keeping rhythm.

examples.ko: 드럼 스틱을 두 개 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought two new drumsticks.

explain: 드럼은 '드럼을 치다'처럼 '치다'와 같이 써요. 연주하는 사람은 '드러머'예요. 바이올린은 '켜다', 플루트는 '불다'를 써서 악기마다 동사가 달라요.

phrases.en: The drummer of that band is really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드럼을 연주하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who plays the drums.

phrases.en: I'm going to learn drums during vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 처음 익힐 때 '배우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 배우다 when you are learning an instrument.

phrases.en: Listening to drum playing makes me excited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드럼을 치는 일 자체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the act of playing the drums.

explain_en: Drums go with '치다': '드럼을 치다'. A person who plays drums is a '드러머'. Each instrument takes its own verb: the violin uses '켜다' and the flute uses '불다'.

examples.en: We learned the recorder in music class.
The recorder has a clear, light sound.
My younger sibling plays an easy song on the recorder.
I don't know where my recorder is.
I took a recorder test when I was in elementary school.

examples.ko: 리코더에 입을 대고 천천히 불어 보세요.
examples.en: Put your mouth on the recorder and blow slowly.

explain: 리코더는 '불다'와 같이 써서 '리코더를 불다'라고 해요. 피아노는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'처럼 악기마다 짝이 되는 동사가 달라요. '리코더를 연주하다'라고도 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I played the recorder in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 입으로 부는 악기라서 '불다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 불다 because you blow into it.

phrases.en: The sound of the recorder is clear.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기의 소리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the instrument's sound.

phrases.en: My younger sibling plays the recorder.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불다'보다 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A bit more formal than 불다.

explain_en: You say 리코더를 불다 (literally, blow the recorder). Each instrument pairs with its own verb: 피아노를 치다 for the piano and 바이올린을 켜다 for the violin. You can also say 리코더를 연주하다.
